clue.text: Explained what one needs to pot seedlings after dark?

definitions.meaning: to explain something is to make it clearer, to illuminate it

definitions.text: what one needs to pot seedlings after dark?
definitions.meaning: a gardener potting at night wants a lamp fitted in the garden hut

explanation.definitionFit: To clarify a matter is idiomatically to illuminate it; read literally, the phrase is a lamp fitted in a garden hut.

clue.text: She's got it coming to her

definitions.text: She's got it coming to her

parts.words: She's got it coming to her
parts.note: sounds like someone due a punishment, but means a woman due to inherit a fortune

explanation.definitionFit: A woman in line to inherit wealth has a legacy due to come to her.

definitions.meaning: a smutty book or piece of writing

explanation.surface: Shady dealings lead to the printing of something indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand deeds are idiomatically grubby tasks; a filthy book is literally a smutty piece of writing.

clue.text: One's holy book needed for religion

parts.note: one is I, and with the 's it gives I'S, read as IS
Lam is the standard abbreviation for Lamentations, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone needs their scripture in order to practise a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy book' suggests the Koran, but it is Lamentations, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim faith founded by the Prophet Muhammad is one of the world's major religions.

indicators.note: to confuse is to jumble, so the word teacher is rearranged here

explanation.surface: A region or subject that baffles the schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of land measure equal to ten thousand square metres, so a measure of area.

parts.note: read as 'unfashionable' plus 'suits' it splits into words for passé and for matches

explanation.definitionFit: Sets of clothes are ensembles such as suits; the split reading gives passé plus matches.

clue.text: Performance history of part of disc, and all of it

parts.note: one song on an album is a track
the whole disc is a record, a vinyl LP

explanation.surface: A singer's past achievements are judged by one song and then the whole album.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's past results or achievements, used to judge future performance.

clue.text: Desire refusal to be reversed as capricious

parts.note: to desire is to want

indicators.note: says the word for refusal is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Wanting a no to be overturned seems whimsical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reversed' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained and wilful, behaving on a whim without reason.

clue.text: More prepared to use book? That's right

parts.note: to use a book is to read it
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are better equipped by studying a book, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of ready: someone more prepared is more set to act.

clue.text: Find commander coming in after midnight

indicators.note: says the commander's letters enter the word for after midnight

parts.note: the small hours count as late at night
OC is Officer Commanding, a military commander

explanation.surface: Tracking down the officer as he arrives home in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts OC inside LATE. 'Commander' wants CO, but here it is OC.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, so the verb means to track down.

parts.note: the aunt is an agony aunt, and her bit of the newspaper is the problem page

explanation.walkthrough: An agony aunt is a newspaper adviser answering readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper section where an adviser replies to readers' troubles.

parts.note: not clothes irons but metal utensils used at home for eating, knives and forks being slang irons

explanation.surface: Pressing clothes around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Knives, forks and spoons are table implements, informally called irons.

definitions.meaning: the sense or significance given of something

explanation.surface: Planning to explain oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Intending is having a purpose in mind; an explanation gives the sense or significance of something.

clue.text: One's slides are icily received at these

definitions.text: One's slides are icily received at these

parts.words: One's slides are icily received at these
parts.note: sounds like a slide show met coldly, but the slides are glides on ice

explanation.surface: A speaker's presentation gets a frosty reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-skating arenas are where people glide over ice.

clue.text: Two cricket sides cross oceans — wrong time for tourists

indicators.note: the two halves of the field straddle the oceans, so they sit on either side

parts.note: the off side of a cricket field
the on side of a cricket field, opposite the off side
oceans are seas

explanation.surface: Cricket teams travelling over the sea at a bad time for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into off side and on side. 'cross' puts SEAS between OFF and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet part of the year when few holidaymakers visit.

clue.text: The limit of spending on public transport

definitions.text: The limit of spending on public transport

parts.words: The limit of spending on public transport
parts.note: sounds like a budget cap, but is a section of a bus route covered by one ticket price

explanation.walkthrough: A British bus route is split into sections; each boundary marks a change in ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a bus route for which a fixed charge applies, its end being a boundary.

parts.note: a building's janitor, read as one who takes trouble

explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building; split, the word suggests someone who takes trouble.

indicators.note: the word for gag is placed around the university

parts.note: to gag is to retch
OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: Tweaking a joke about a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OU (the Open University, a British distance-learning institution) inside RETCH. 'gag' looks like a joke but is to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch up is to make small improvements, as to a photograph.

indicators.note: composing is arranging, so the words notes in are put together anew

explanation.surface: Writing music under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composing' rearranges the letters of NOTES IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress or tightness, as in a stretched rope or a fraught situation.

parts.note: sounds like a storm brewing, but is digestive gas pains

explanation.definitionFit: Severe abdominal pain, often from trapped gas, especially in babies.

clue.text: Funny mineral seen in mountain pass

indicators.note: says the mineral appears within the pass

parts.note: a col is a pass between peaks
mica is a mineral

explanation.surface: An amusing rock spotted high in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing or laughable, a synonym for humorous.

clue.text: Long and narrow lake I approach

parts.note: to approach is to near

explanation.surface: Someone nears a slender stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in or like a line, stretched out lengthwise.

indicators.note: badly fitting suggests something out of place, so the word denture is rearranged

explanation.surface: Correcting false teeth that don't sit right.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned again, as a piano or radio, so altered to fit.

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the European goes around the clubs

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A friendly continental visiting nightspots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts DANE around C. 'Social' is a noun, a party, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a party, and a ball is such a gathering.

clue.text: Extremely important symbol of office minister received

indicators.note: says the seal takes in the minister, holding it inside

parts.note: a seal is an emblem of authority

explanation.surface: A government official is handed the mark of authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly influential and formative, shaping later developments.

indicators.note: says the author's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.surface: A writer read out as trouble afoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recited' gives a word sounding like BUNYAN, the 17th-century author.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the big toe joint, a foot complaint.

parts.note: to call is to claim, as in calling a win

explanation.surface: Hailing a Tory candidate's shout.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise loudly or applaud, to hail.

indicators.note: developed means changed and grown, so the words hence taller are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mushroom that has grown bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of HENCE TALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow edible wild mushroom prized in cooking.
